source.notes: Scanned school paper (no text layer apart from the icseboard.org watermark); OCR corrected against the page images. Printed header: Grade IX, Assessment I, English Language. Paper - I, Time: 2 Hours, M.M: 80. No year is printed; examYear 2024 is taken from the file name (...-300924-2024) and the icseboard.org folder. No school name printed. Q1 (any one of a-e, [20]) and Q2 (any one of two letters, [10]) are stored one entry per option with a shared choiceGroup. Q3 [10] (notice and email) carries one group mark and is kept as one entry. Q4: the motel passage (over 250 words) is not reproduced; 4(i) [2] (two vocabulary MCQs) is one entry; 4(iii) a-e carry their own marks. Q5 (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) each carry only a group mark ([4], [4], [4], [8]) and are kept as one entry each with the items/options in the text. The picture for Q1(e) is not reproduced. A promotional box (WhatsApp number, partly Hindi) on page 5 is not part of the paper and is ignored. Paper's own errors ('for ended up', 'shall go to the play' without 'I', 'as too play') kept as printed. No answer key.

questions.text:
Join the following sentences to make one complete sentence without using and, but or so. Choose the correct option.
1. Who has snatched the boy's laptop? The police will soon find out.
(a) The police will soon find who has snatched the boy's laptop.
(b) The police will soon find out the boy's laptop.
(c) The police will soon find out who snatched the boy's laptop.
(d) The police would soon find out the snatcher of the boy's laptop.
2. The boy is still very weak. He must not play football yet.
(a) The boy is still not strong enough to play football.
(b) The boy is too weak as too play football.
(c) The boy is weak on to play football.
(d) The boy is yet weak to play football.
3. Pull the chain. The train will stop.
(a) Pull the chain when the train will stop.
(b) The train will stop to pull the chain.
(c) The train will stop if you pull the chain.
(d) The train stops after pulling the chain.
4. He can go there. He has to tell his warden about it.
(a) He needs to tell his warden before going there.
(b) He have to tell his warden as he goes there.
(c) He has to tell his warden before he goes there.
(d) He had to tell his warden before he goes there.

questions.text:
Rewrite the following sentences according to the instructions given after each make other changes that may be necessary, but do not change the meaning of each sentence. Choose the correct options.
1. Everyone wants to become rich. (Begin with: Who ...)
(a) Who wants not to be rich?
(b) Who does not wants riches?
(c) Who does not want richness?
(d) Who does not want to become rich?
2. The little boy hid himself so that he might not be seen. (Use: otherwise)
(a) The little boy hid himself otherwise he would have been seen.
(b) Had he not hid himself otherwise the little boy must have been seen.
(c) The little boy was himself hidden otherwise he was being seen.
(d) The little boy hid otherwise he might not be seen.
3. Run fast, else you will miss the bus. (Begin with: If ...)
(a) If you cannot run fast, you will miss the bus.
(b) If you do not run fast, you will miss the bus.
(c) If you do not run fast, else you will miss the bus.
(d) If you want not to miss the bus, run fast.
4. Work hard and you will succeed. (Begin with: Unless ...)
(a) Unless do not work hard, you will succeed.
(b) Unless should you work hard, you will not succeed.
(c) Unless you work hard, you will not succeed.
(d) Unless when you work hard, you will not succeed.
5. He said to me, "Are you going to the restaurant tonight?" (Begin with: He inquired
(a) He enquired if I was going to the restaurant tonight.
(b) He enquired from me of going to the restaurant tonight.
(c) He enquired whether I was going to the restaurant tonight.
(d) He enquired whether I was going to the restaurant that night.
6. shall go to the play if you come. (End: .... unless you come.)
(a) I will go to the play unless you come.
(b) I shall go to the play unless you do not come.
(c) I will not go to the play unless you can come.
(d) I shall not go to the play unless you come.
7. No other king was as wise as Ashoka. (Use: wiser)
(a) Ashoka was wiser than any other king.
(b) No other king is wiser to Ashoka.
(c) No other king was wiser as Ashoka.
(d) No other king as wiser as Ashoka was.
8. The pianist performed admirably on the stage. (Begin with: The pianist's ...)
(a) The pianist's performance on the stage was admirable.
(b) The pianist's admirably performed at the stage.
(c) The pianist's admirable performance was on the stage.
(d) The pianist's stage was admirable for the performance.
